primary_sources: Pandas & NumPy Enterprise Data Wrangling Standards
Harvard CS109 Exploratory Data Analysis Guidelines

rules.explanation: Dropping rows with missing values naively introduces bias, while improper imputation can alter distribution statistics.
rules.do: Analyze missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and apply domain-aware imputation (e.g., median, KNN, iterative imputation) or create explicit missingness flags.
rules.dont: Do not drop all null rows indiscriminately or fill missing numerical values with arbitrary constant zeroes without statistical justification.

rules.explanation: Extreme outliers distort statistical summaries, mean-variance metrics, and regression trends if left unexamined.
rules.do: Identify outliers using robust statistical methods (e.g., IQR bounds, Z-score thresholds, Isolation Forests) and handle them appropriately via capping, transformation, or deletion.
rules.dont: Do not remove outliers blindly without investigating whether they represent valid extreme domain events or sensor errors.

rules.explanation: Univariate analysis alone fails to uncover multi-collinearity or hidden interaction effects between variables.
rules.do: Evaluate pairwise feature correlations (e.g., Pearson, Spearman), Variance Inflation Factor (VIF), and distribution skews prior to modeling.
rules.dont: Do not assume feature independence without verifying correlation matrices and collinearity metrics.

rules.rule_name: Automated Type Casting and Schema Validation
rules.explanation: Operating on incorrectly parsed data types (e.g., dates stored as strings, numeric values as objects) leads to incorrect calculations and performance bottlenecks.
rules.do: Enforce explicit dtypes, parse dates accurately, and convert categorical string features to categorical memory-efficient structures early in ingestion.
rules.dont: Do not leave numerical or temporal variables stored as raw generic object columns in dataframes.
